about.title: Hughson Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Hughson's economy runs on agriculture, food processing, and the trucking and distribution work tied to corridors like Hatch Road and Whitmore Avenue. That means job sites here often mix heavy equipment, delivery vehicles, and outside contractors — a setup that raises real questions about who's responsible when someone gets hurt. In most cases, California workers' compensation is the only path against your own employer, no matter who caused the accident. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on the road contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may also be possible. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly — we simply connect injured workers in Hughson with an independent attorney who can look at the details, explain your options, and help you understand the deadlines that apply. There's no cost to get that conversation started, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Hughson Workers Look Into a Third-Party Claim

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Full Picture
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, but it doesn't cover a negligent third party like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker. An independent attorney can help sort out whether one applies to your situation.

items.title: Two Separate Clocks Are Running
items.desc: You generally need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, while a third-party injury claim in California carries its own 2-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Retaliation for Reporting Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers who report an on-the-job injury. If you're worried about your job while dealing with an injury, an attorney can explain your protections.

items.question: I was hurt while driving for work near Hatch Road or Whitmore Avenue — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: If another driver caused the crash while you were working, you may have both a workers' compensation claim and a separate third-party claim against that driver. These aren't mutually exclusive, and an independent attorney can help you understand how they interact. LawProactive can connect you with someone who handles both types of cases.

items.question: My employer in Hughson says I can't sue them — is that true?
items.answer: Generally, yes — California workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, even if they were careless. However, this rule doesn't protect other parties who may have contributed to your injury, like a contractor or equipment supplier. A free consultation can clarify whether a third party is involved in your case.

items.question: What if I'm afraid my employer will retaliate if I report my injury?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting a job injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, that itself may be worth discussing with an attorney. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who handles these situations.
